title: Abstract presents the p-bar=1/2 special case as the method's general reduction
quote: the method is a single expression whose exponent reduces to $\gamma=z\sqrt{2+z^2}$
explanation: Eq. (13) gives the general exponent as gamma = [z*sqrt(2 + 4*p_bar*(1-p_bar)*z^2)] clipped, and Eq. (15) states gamma = z*sqrt(2+z^2) only 'At the default p_bar = 1/2'. The abstract drops that condition, so a reader takes the two-term form to be the method rather than one point in a p_bar-indexed family. The paper is precise about this in the body; only the abstract loses the qualifier.
missing_evidence: a statement that the two-term form holds only at the default base rate
allowed_wording: whose exponent reduces, at the default base rate p_bar = 1/2, to gamma = z*sqrt(2+z^2)
forbidden_wording: whose exponent reduces to gamma = z*sqrt(2+z^2)

evidence_anchor.text: Eq. (13) general form vs Eq. (15) p_bar=1/2 form

title: 'No tuned constant anywhere' coexists with four variant-specific constants, and the clip decides every headline cell
quote: one probit and one square root, with no tuned constant anywhere
explanation: Four constants are set by hand and differ across the two variants the paper ships: nu_dev = 1.28 vs nu_LF = 2.33, and gamma_max = 4 (dev) vs 2 (label-free). The paper defends them as 'a significance level' and 'a clip' fixed before data, which is fair for nu, but results/tact_eval.json shows the clip is not inert: TACT-dev = +/-4.0 and TACT-LF = +/-2.0 exactly, i.e. gamma == gamma_max, in all four sweep cells reported as 1.000 (kappa = +/-0.4, +/-0.6) and in all three monotone-distortion cells. The derived expression is load-bearing only in the mid-range cells, which are the cells where TACT loses to SignGrid-dev. The paper itself concedes the cap is doing work when it attributes TACT-LF beating TACT-dev in the grouped cell to 'its lower exponent cap ($2$ vs.\ $4$) regularizes better'.
missing_evidence: disclosure that gamma is saturated at the clip in the winning cells
allowed_wording: no constant is tuned on the evaluation data; nu is a significance level and gamma_max a clip fixed in advance, though in the saturated cells the clip rather than the link determines the exponent

title: 'Beats the oracle over the entire raw-value weight family' rests on a 9-point grid whose maximum is its own boundary
quote: ``Oracle'' is the test-set best over \emph{raw-value} weight policies; rank invariance beats that entire family under compression.
explanation: The oracle is implemented in experiments/run_tact_eval.py as max over SIGN_GRID = [-4.0, -2.0, -1.0, -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0], nine points. For monotone_compress, results/tact_eval.json records oracle = {acc: 0.965, gamma: 4.0}: the argmax sits at the largest exponent in the grid, so no evidence bounds the family at gamma > 4, and the grid has no point between 2 and 4. 'That entire family' is a claim about a continuum; the evidence is a coarse grid truncated exactly where the maximum lands. The paper never states the grid in the text.
missing_evidence: the grid stated in the text
allowed_wording: beats the best raw-value weight policy over the nine-point signed exponent grid evaluated here
forbidden_wording: beats the oracle over the entire raw-value weight family

title: Abstract's 'all of which the method survived' omits the flagship variant's documented catastrophic failure
quote: all of which the method survived
explanation: The abstract's closing claim is literally true of the four pre-registered falsifiers, which were scoped to the sweep. But the paper's own Discussion reports that TACT-LF, the variant the abstract credits with the 1.000-vs-0.807 recovery, in a paraphrased wrong-majority cell 'mis-signs, saturates at $\gamma=-2.0$, and scores $0.000$ against an \SC{} floor of $0.340$', and that 'None of the four alarms fires'. A reader who stops at the abstract forms a materially wrong belief about the failure envelope. One clause fixes it, and omitting it converts the paper's real honesty into apparent concealment.
missing_evidence: abstract-level statement of the rho_bar > 1/2 unguarded failure
allowed_wording: all four pre-registered falsifiers survived; a post-hoc paraphrased-majority cell outside the pre-registered sweep was not survived, and no alarm fires there
forbidden_wording: all of which the method survived

evidence_anchor.text: Sec. VII, conditional label-free guarantee paragraph

title: 'Two real-trace campaigns confirm the premise' when the first measured discrimination in the wrong direction
quote: Two real-trace campaigns on a frozen model confirm the premise and locate the binding constraint
explanation: Campaign 1 (GSM8K/CommonsenseQA) measured D-hat = -0.219 with SE = 0.176, z = -1.24: not significant and pointing the wrong way, which the paper states plainly in Sec. V-G and correctly reads as confirming its null-direction prediction. What campaign 1 confirms is that calibration is uninformative about voting utility, not the premise that the channel carries signed discrimination. The abstract's plural 'campaigns ... confirm the premise' invites the reader to credit both campaigns with the positive finding that only the second one supports.
missing_evidence: a positive within-item discrimination measurement in campaign 1
allowed_wording: one real-trace campaign confirms the premise on competition mathematics; the other confirms the null-direction prediction and the calibration-discrimination argument
forbidden_wording: Two real-trace campaigns on a frozen model confirm the premise

title: Conclusion promises an exact CISC fallback that the shipped feature map does not provide
quote: plain self-consistency when the evidence is absent and CISC when it is at full strength
explanation: Proposition 2 delivers exact CISC-power equivalence only under the log-value feature map, 'With the feature map $\varphi^{\log}_{q,i}=\log c_{q,i}-\overline{\log c_q}$'. The shipped method uses the van der Waerden rank score of Eq. (2), and the paper's own C1 makes rank-only dependence the source of its monotone-invariance claim, so the two feature maps are mutually exclusive. As shipped, TACT has one exact anchor (bitwise SC at gamma = 0, a shared code path), not two. The abstract is more careful here ('a log-value feature map reproduces CISC-power'); the Conclusion drops the condition and states the fallback as a property of the method.
missing_evidence: an exact CISC reduction for the van der Waerden feature map actually shipped
allowed_wording: plain self-consistency when the evidence is absent, and, under a log-value feature map, CISC when it is at full strength
forbidden_wording: exact fallbacks at both ends, plain self-consistency when the evidence is absent and CISC when it is at full strength

title: 'Three times the SC floor' for a 2.93x ratio
quote: the best result in the field ($0.585$; three times the \SC{} floor)
explanation: 0.585 / 0.200 = 2.925. Rounding 2.93x up to 'three times' is trivial in most papers, but this one stakes its case on reporting margins honestly, including its own losses to a trivial baseline. A reviewer who checks one arithmetic claim and finds it rounded in the author's favour discounts the others.
allowed_wording: 0.585, nearly three times the SC floor
